head.info: A structure is a named way to handle an order: its steps, its team, its people in the office. A rule says which orders use it: the list is read from the top and the first rule that fits wins, so an exception is a more exact rule above. An order that is not started follows the rules; at the first print it keeps what it has.

rule.added: The rule is added at its place.
rule.closed: The rule is closed and kept.

structure.closed: The structure {name} is closed and kept.

failed: The order structures could not be read.

rules.title: Rules
rules.answer: The first rule that fits wins. A new order takes its structure by itself. An order in work never changes.
rules.first: It is the first rule already.
rules.last: It is the last rule already.
rules.dead: A rule above takes all its orders. So this rule never fits.
rules.deadBecause: Rule {n} above takes all its orders. So this rule never fits.
rules.normalWayHint: the route of the product · the team by hand, as today
rules.readOnly: The owner and sales change the rules.

rule.when: When an order line is from
rule.whenCustomer: When an order line is from
rule.title: Rule {n}
rule.makeOneFirst: Or make one first: Structures › New structure….
rule.managerMakes: The production manager makes a structure.
rule.fitsNone: No open order fits it now. It waits for the next order.
rule.place: It goes to place {n}, above the first rule that would take its orders.
rule.placeLast: It goes to place {n}, the last place before “Everything else”.
rule.keptNote: An order in work keeps what it started with. Only orders that are not started take a change.
rule.note: A note for your colleagues (not needed)
rule.noteHint: For example: agreed with the customer in March

held.closed: This structure is closed: choose an open one.
held.same: Rule {n} is for exactly these orders: change that rule.

try.title: Try an order
try.answer: Choose a customer and a category: the rule that wins, and why the others do not. Nothing is saved.
try.noRule: No rule fits: the normal way

how.title: How it works
how.structure: A structure is a named way to handle an order: its route, its team, its people in the office.
how.rule: A rule says “orders like this use that structure”. The first rule that fits wins. An exception is a more exact rule above.
how.order: One order by hand: on the order, Production › Order structure › “Another structure for this order…”, with a reason.
how.kept: An order that is not started follows the rules. At the first print it keeps what it has.

structures.title: Structures
structures.answer: A rule points to one. The production manager makes a structure.
structures.noTeam: No team: given by hand, as today
structures.readOnly: The production manager makes and changes a structure. You choose which orders use it.

structure.title: Structure · {name}
structure.readOnly: You read this structure. The production manager changes its team and its people. You choose which orders use it: with a rule, or on one order.
structure.name: Its name
structure.stepsHint: Each line follows the route of its product (product › Route).
structure.teamsUnread: The teams could not be read.

teams.none: No team: the production manager gives the order to a team by hand, as today.
teams.one: The order goes to this team at Confirm.
teams.many: These teams work together. The first one you chose is in charge.

structure.peopleUnread: The office people could not be read.
structure.peopleHint: They join the order and its chat at Confirm. A person joins only the orders of a customer that the person works for.
structure.keptNote: A change goes to the orders that are not started.

held.name: Type a name first.
held.taken: A structure with this name is there already. Type another name.

order.title: Order structure
order.failed: The order structure could not be read.
order.noLines: This order has no line yet.
order.normalKept: The normal way. Kept since the work started.
order.many_one: {count} structure on this order: each line follows its own.
order.many_other: {count} structures on this order: each line follows its own.
order.manyKept_one: {count} structure on this order, kept since the work started.
order.manyKept_other: {count} structures on this order, kept since the work started.
order.byHand: Or choose by hand, for this order only
order.whyHint: For example: a show piece, the race team makes it

held.pick: Choose a structure or the normal way.
held.why: Say why this order is different.

customer.title: How its orders are handled
customer.noneHint: Its orders go the normal way, or follow a rule for every customer.
customer.failed: The rules of this customer could not be read.

error.write: It was not saved. Try again.
error.offline: No answer from the factory: check the network and try again.
error.notFound: It is not there any more.
error.conflict: Someone changed this meanwhile: it was read again. Check it and try again.
error.invalid: It was refused as it is: check what you chose.
